subject: Escape hatch options and feature-accordion for plan selection
messages:
From: Oliver Stone <oliver@healthlytics.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Patel <priya@healthlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Escape hatch & feature-accordion for plan selection

Diego —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick follow up from our side: we're trying to map out how a mid-year downshift would look if our usage drops (likely in Q3). Two main asks: 1) Is there a formal "escape hatch" we can use to temporarily reduce committed capacity without financial lock-in? 2) How does Redwood handle feature-bundles when customers step down tiers (which features remain, which are gated behind upgrades)?

Context: we're on the Enterprise Core plan (12 reserved GPUs equivalent) with a two-year commitment. We're not looking to break the contract, just want a safe path to reduce spend during a seasonal downturn and preserve critical features (especially KV caching and model pinning).

Attached: current_contract_summary.pdf (PDF)

Can you outline concrete options and any timing/approval requirements? Also cc'd Priya (ops) — she'll own the technical constraints if we need to stage the ramp down.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Stone
Head of ML Platform, Healthlytics
oliver@healthlytics.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Patel <priya@healthlytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escape hatch & feature-accordion for plan selection

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below are three pragmatic paths we typically offer; I'll loop Ben for discount/approval and Marissa for any contract exceptions. Short answers first: yes, we have guardrails for temporary capacity stepdowns ("Flex Pause"), and we can map a feature-accordion that preserves essential runtime capabilities during a stepdown.

Options (high-level):

1) Flex Pause (preferred for seasonality)
   - Duration: up to 3 months pause on reserved throughput with repriced on-demand fall-back.
   - Impact: preserves model pinning and dev access; KV cache is retained (cold) but persisted for quick restart.
   - Financial: one-time pause fee (pro-rated) + minimum monthly retainment (~15% of committed cost).

2) Stepdown with StepCredits
   - Duration: longer-term reduction (3–12 months) with stepdown credits applied to future usage.
   - Impact: some non-critical add-ons (priority routing, expanded tracing retention) move to a paid add-on while core inference and pinning remain.
   - Financial: tiered credits based on reduced commit — requires manager approval for >20% discount.

3) Feature accordion (slice features, keep essentials)
   - Keep: model pinning, basic KV cache, function calling support.
   - Remove (example): advanced trace retention, extended eval retention, some high-throughput priority lanes.
   - Mechanic: temporary amendment attached to contract, opt-in per feature.

Next steps I recommend: 1) quick internal review with Ben on commercial terms (cc'd), 2) technical call with Priya to confirm which features absolutely must stay, 3) we draft an amendment (1–2 page) with the selected path.

I've attached a short workbook (proposed_paths.xlsx) showing sample math for a 30% and 50% reduction. If you want, I can propose a staged schedule to avoid a hard drop.

I'll hold on the formal amendment until Ben confirms commercial levers.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | diego_fernandez@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Oliver Stone <oliver@healthlytics.com>, Priya Patel <priya@healthlytics.com>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escape hatch & feature-accordion for plan selection

Diego / Oliver —

Thanks for laying this out. From a commercial perspective I can sign off on the following concessions without escalation:

- One-time pause fee waived for a single 30-day Flex Pause within a 12-month window.
- Approve up to 15% temporary credit on committed spend for pauses up to 3 months.
- Feature accordion allowed; core inference, model pinning, and KV persistence guaranteed.

If Healthlytics requests a >15% credit or a >30% long-term stepdown we need Marissa's approval (copied). For modeling: for your RWI-2028-4478 deal, a 30% stepdown translates to a 12% effective discount over the year (numbers in Diego's workbook).

If you confirm which path (Flex Pause vs Stepdown), I'll prepare a one-page amendment and a DocuSign envelope to keep turnaround < 72 hours.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Oliver —

Following Ben and Diego's notes: I can approve a one-time concession to support Healthlytics through a seasonal dip. We will:

- Approve a single 60-day Flex Pause window with a reduced retainment fee (10% of committed cost) and guaranteed KV persistence.
- Offer a 15% stepdown credit for reductions of up to 30% for up to 3 months. Anything beyond that requires a renewal discussion.

Attached is the amendment (amendment_escape_hatch_v1.pdf). Please review and confirm acceptance. Once you sign, Ben will trigger the DocuSign link and ops (Priya) and our infra team will queue the pause schedule.
